identity.title: Characterization of the SsdA deaminase-family for improved cytosine base editors.

content.abstract: The choice of a suitable cytosine deaminase is a key decision when designing a base editor. Recently, bacterial toxins with cytosine deaminase activity have been established to build potent base editors for genome editing. Among those, SsdA gained considerable traction, being highly active and among the smallest established deaminases for cytosine base editors. The toxic nature of SsdA presents the major challenge, making wild type SsdA unsuitable for base editing. Although several modifications of SsdA are available, a comparison and deeper understanding of these modifications is still missing. Here, we investigate and compare the effects of several SsdA modifications. We enable a more educated choice for researchers by characterizing several improved SsdA variants for base editing. Amino acid substitutions at a key residue in SsdA suggest that steric alterations relieve its toxic effects. Indeed, the in vitro deaminase activity of SsdA was negatively linked to its in vivo performance. This indicates that base editing performance is highly compromised by toxic side effects, making less active deaminase variants the better genome editing tools. We further characterized a set of SsdA homologous proteins and showed that they were similarly toxic as SsdA. Two of them were confirmed to be cytosine deaminases and one of these allowed the construction of a new, highly functional base editing tool. This work deepens our understanding on DYW-family cytosine deaminases and broadens their use for genome editing.
